title: Frontend: Secret Code Shuffler
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Secret Code Shuffler. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({text,shift}). Shift ASCII letters by the integer shift modulo 26, preserving case and every nonletter. This reversible toy code is not encryption.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.

Treat this original exercise as a Caesar-style shift, not encryption: normalize the shift modulo the alphabet size, map only supported letters, and preserve other characters according to the contract.
alternativeApproaches: Distinguish this toy substitution from authenticated encryption and avoid presenting obfuscation as security.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Shift zero; wrap at Z; negative shift.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
